description: Output and technology grow while inequality ecological pressure and fragility intensify.
Climate investment industrial policy and public goods support low-carbon development.
Geopolitical conflict debt pressure and low investment weaken development futures.
Advanced sectors expand rapidly while workers and regions without access fall behind.
Debt service and expensive capital reduce public investment and policy space.
Public investment in health education care and social protection raises development quality.
Commodity growth creates revenue but limits diversification and ecological viability.
Regional supply chains industrial policy and resilience investment strengthen development.
